 (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.5853/2022  JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed claim application U/Sec 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by her in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the petitioner case as follows:-
On 25.08.2022 at about 05.30 a.m, the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on Bajaj CT 100 Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-02-JJ-2696 and the same was driving by one Ullas.D on the extreme left side/edge of Kamadihalli - Nagamangala Road, at high speed, in rash and negligent manner, when they reached near Mahadeshwara Hill/Betta, Kumbarakoppalu

, the Motor Cycle slipped towards road side slope,
thereby the petitioner and rider fell down along with the Motor Cycle and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident she was shifted to Pulse Multi Speciality hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as inpatient on 25.08.2022 and discharged on 10.09.2022 with an advice to take complete bed rest, continue medicines and to take follow-up treatment as an outpatient and (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 she is still under follow-up treatment as an outpatient and she has spent Rs.2,75,000/- towards hospital charges, medicines, conveyance and other incidental expenses.
Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and was aged about 19 years and was doing Tailoring work beside household work and earning more than Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, she is unable to do any physical strain work till this day and undergoing huge pecuniary loss, great mental shock, agony and financial loss.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent Sanjana .D vs Gangadharappa .M on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199500888/
2 riding of the aforesaid offending Motor Cycle by its rider and in this regard the Bindiganavile Police have registered a case against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Motor Cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.

03. Earlier the petitioner has filed claim petition against respondents No.1 and 2, but the respondent No.1 RC owner was died on 12.07.2019 itself leaving behind his LRs and they are not been transferred the said offending Motor Cycle in their names.
Hence, the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 petitioner has impleaded the said LRs as respondent Nos.1(a) and (b).
On service of notice, respondents No.1(a) and (b) and respondent No.2 have appeared before this tribunal, but only the respondent No.2 has filed objections.

04. Respondent No.2 in its objection denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that this court may be pleased to consider recent amendment pertaining to pay and recover 2019 and not to pass the Judgment and award to "pay and recover" from the owner.

This respondent denies existence of policy in respect of the vehicle bearing No.KA-02-JJ-2696 of the respondent No.1 and contended that the compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant and the rider of the offending vehicle rode the same without having driving licence at the material time of accident, which is in contravention of the policy condition and also M.V. Act and there is inordinate delay of one day in lodging the complaint and there is no fitness certificate (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 and permit ot the vehicle of the respondent No.1 to ply the vehicle on the road at the material time of the accident and it is clear violation of policy condition and entire negligence is on the part of the petitioner to cause the accident and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that she has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 25.08.2022 at about 05.30 a.m, on Kumbarakoppalu,
Kamadihalli to Nagamangala Road, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya, due to rash and negligent act of riding of the Bike bearing registration No. KA-02-JJ-2696 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03

. What Order or Award?
Sanjana .D vs Gangadharappa .M on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199500888/
3 06.

In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 17 (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 and closed her side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined its Manager Legal as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.

08. Heard both sides.
09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In affirmative  Issue No.2 In partly affirmative  Issue No.3

As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- Petitioner filed affidavit as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments.

Though, she has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent riding of the offending Motor Cycle by its rider, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
On perusal of the (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Bindiganavile Police against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent riding of the offending Motor Cycle the accident was occurred.
Due to this impact, the petitioner sustained injuries.
11. The accident took place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor Cycle.

Ex.P.3 is Crime details form and Ex.P.4 is Spot Mahazar showing the place of accident at Kumbarakoppalu Village, Bindiganavile Hobli, on Kamadihalli - Nelamangala Road, near Mahadeshwara Hill, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is IMV report which discloses that involvement of offending Motor Cycle in the accident.

Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate which shows that the petitioner sustained 1) muscle deep abraded laceration 20 x 10 cm over medial aspect of left leg with loss of skin, tibia bone, ankle discruption and injury to tibial vessels and muscles, 2) bone deep abrasion over dorsum of left foot 5 x 3 cm, 3) muscle deep abrasion over lower 1/3 left thigh 10 x 5 cm, 4) multiple muscle deep abrasion over right lower limb 5th toe, knee ( 3 x 5 cm), thigh (5 x 5 cm) and 5) muscle deep abrasion over both hands and face, out of which injury No.1 is (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.5853/2022
grievous in nature and rest are simple in nature.
Ex.P.7 is the important document of Investigation Officer.
After completion of the investigation filed Charge sheet against rider of the offending Motor Cycle by name Ullasa.D for the offences punishable U/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.8 is the Discharge summary which shows that the petitioner sustained multiple deep abrasions over left leg with neurovascular injury with bone joint injury and left leg post traumatic raw area.
Ex.P.9 is Sanjana .D vs Gangadharappa .M

on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199500888/
4 Aadhaar card of the petitioner.

The petitioner got examined Medical Record Officer at Pulse Multi Speciality hospital, Bengaluru, as PW.3 and he has produced Authorization letter, MLC, Police intimation and Case sheet as per Ex.P.14 to 17.

To disprove the petitioner case, the respondent No.2 got examined its Manager Legal as RW.1 and he has filed affidavit and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the objections averments.

During his cross- examination he admits that at the time of accident the policy was valid and Police have filed Charge sheet against their insured Motor Cycle and nowhere they have not challeged the Charge sheet.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that the petitioner sustained (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 grievous injuries in a road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Motor Cycle.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

Petitioner in her evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident she was hale and healthy and was aged about 19 years and was doing Tailoring work beside household work and earning more than Rs.20,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.2,75,000/- towards hospital charges, medicines,
conveyance and other incidental expenses.
Due to accidental injuries, she is unable to do any physical strain work till this day and undergoing huge pecuniary loss, great mental shock, agony and financial loss.
13. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, she has not produced any documents.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory documents in proof of the income of the injured, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 accident of the year 2022 to be taken as Rs.15,500/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal assessed the monthly income of petitioner is at Rs.15,500/-.
14.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief-examination that the petitioner has sustained multiple deep abrasions over the left leg with neurovascular injury and bone injury and post traumatic raw area over the foot and ankle and he assessed physical disability of the left lower limb at 33% and whole body physical disability at 11% and he has produced Clinical report and X-ray as per Ex.P.12 and 13.
15.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
As per Ex.P.8 Discharge summary, the petitioner was admitted as inpatient at Pulse Multi Speciality hospital, Bengaluru, for 16 days.
During the aforesaid period, the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, she is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
(SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 Sanjana .D vs Gangadharappa .M on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199500888/
5 16. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 Doctor and as per Clinical report, Case sheet and X-ray and on account of accidental injuries
, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by her in the accident, she is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
17. Loss of income during laid up period:-
As already discussed above, this tribunal has assessed the income of Rs.15,500/- per month and he was admitted in the hospital for 16 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of her stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation for atleast three months.

Thus,
taking into account the income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.46,500/-
(Rs.15,500/- x 3) under this head.
18. Medical Expenses:-
The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.10 for Rs.6,08,779/- and Prescriptions as per Ex.P.11.

On perusal of Ex.P.10, it is noticed that Sl. Nos.5, 6,
9, 10, 13, 15, 17, 19, 22, 23, 24, 28, 29 (which is same bill of 26), 30, 38, 39 and 44 and Sl. Nos.1 and 2 Rs.154/- and Rs.160/- are included in Sl. Nos.42 and 43,
hence (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 the said amount of Rs.2,51,409/- has to be deducted in total amount.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondent No.2 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,57,370/- under this head.

19. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.

20. Looking to the nature of the injuries, it is duty of petitioner to prove her age, but petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show her exact date of birth.
However, she has produced Aadhaar card at Ex.P.9.

Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age for any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 08.06.2004 and the alleged accident was occurred on 25.08.2022.

Therefore,
considering the said document, this tribunal has assessed the age of (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 the petitioner as 19 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is '18'.

sentences.text: If the petitioner is having self employee, a future prospectus has to be considered.
The petitioner was aged 19 years comes in the age group of below 40 years on the date of accident and was self employee, hence 40% has to be added as Rs.15,500 + 6,200/- = 21,700/-.

Sanjana .D vs Gangadharappa .M on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199500888/
6
The doctor PW.2 has given disability of 33% and 11% pertaining to whole body.

In his cross- examination he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally and he has not seen the Case sheet and old X-rays who treated the petitioner and he has not taken any opinion from the treated doctor.
There is no implants and ankle bone is only fracture and injuries are healed and fractures are united.
However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 11%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
 Rs.21,700/- x 12 x 18 x 11/100 =
Rs.5,15,592/-.
22.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of compensation Amount in No. Rs.
1. Loss of future income 5,15,592-00 2.
Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00 3.
Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and conveyance  charges 4.
Medical Expenses 3,57,370-00 5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00  unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 46,500-00  period  Total 10,09,462-00 23.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.10,09,462/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

Regarding liability:- On service of notice, respondent No.1(a) and (b) have appeared, but not filed objections and not contested the matter and respondent No.2 examined its Manager Legal as RW.1 and admitted issuance of policy of the offending Motor Cycle and its validity, but not disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove their contentions.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1(a) and (b) and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

7 25.
Issue No.3:-

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,09,462/- (Rupees Ten lakhs nine thousand (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.5853/2022 four hundred and sixty two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2, shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The petitioner is at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
